questions.question: A model artifact is 40 MiB. What does that prove about peak runtime memory?
options: Peak memory is exactly 40 MiB
Peak memory is always four times larger
Nothing by itself; weights, tensors, delegates, copies, and the host app must be measured
The model will fit any phone with more than 40 MiB of free storage
questions.explanation: Storage size and peak working memory are different quantities. Profile the integrated application on the target cohort.

questions.question: A process has 512 MiB available and reserves 25% for headroom. Its app baseline is 180 MiB and model peak is 220 MiB. Does the guarded memory gate pass?
options: Yes, with 112 MiB spare
No; the guarded ceiling is 384 MiB and demand is 400 MiB
Yes, because the model peak is below 512 MiB
It depends only on model accuracy
questions.explanation: The guarded ceiling is 512 × 0.75 = 384 MiB. Combined measured demand is 180 + 220 = 400 MiB.

questions.question: Why should warm p95 latency be measured on each hardware and runtime cohort?
options: A single desktop average already predicts every device
Only model file size affects latency
Backend placement, unsupported operators, thermal throttling, and host-app contention vary by cohort
p95 removes the need for a product deadline
questions.explanation: Tail latency is produced by the whole integrated path and can change with device, backend, runtime, and sustained load.

questions.question: What must happen after INT8 quantization before release?
options: Assume a fixed speedup and quality loss
Re-measure compatibility, resource use, latency, energy, thermal behavior, and task quality on representative cohorts
Delete the floating-point evaluation baseline
Skip slice-level quality checks because the artifact is smaller
questions.explanation: Quantization changes representation, but its operational and quality effects are model- and hardware-specific.

questions.question: A canary cohort loses telemetry while the model appears healthy. What should the release controller do?
options: Promote because no failures are visible
Wait until 100% rollout to collect more data
Freeze promotion until observability is restored
Replace p95 latency with an estimated score
questions.explanation: Missing evidence is not passing evidence. Promotion must stop when required fleet signals disappear.

questions.question: What makes an edge model rollback usable during a network outage?
options: A dashboard link to the old version
A signed, compatible known-good artifact retained and tested on the device
A larger cloud autoscaling group
An unbounded local telemetry queue
questions.explanation: Offline recovery requires the device to already possess and verify a compatible fallback, or to use a deterministic non-ML path.
